jobs.goal: The Bash hook gates commits without rewriting commands
jobs.brief: hooks/register.tsx:328 puts a git() shell function in front of every Bash command whose text contains the word "commit" (gated(), line 107). Auto mode reviewed the original command, sees a different one, and gives no verdict, so calls have to be sent again; harmless commands like `grep commit` are rewritten too. Instead: a parser in hooks/shell.ts (beside movesClaims etc.) finds whether the command runs `git commit` and in which directory (`git -C dir commit`, `cd dir && git commit`, global options skipped as gated() does today). If it does, the hook runs `gmod gate-commit --dir <dir>` itself before next(): a refusal becomes deny with the gate's text, a pass runs the command exactly as written. Every other command runs unchanged. Remove gated(). Not in scope: commits hidden inside scripts or make targets (the shell function caught those; a git pre-commit hook could later), and the Edit/Write guards, which never rewrite.

A person approving from a session that is working a job (its folder on gmod/<job>, or a job worktree) is refused every time. Instead, build the decision commit off the checkout: on main's tip (local main, or origin/main when that is ahead), with a temporary index (read-tree, hash-object, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree), and hand that commit to publishDecision (lib/ci.mjs:591), which today pushes HEAD, so it pushes the given commit as gmod/plan-<sha> / the decision branch. The proposal's base is checked against the plan in that main commit, not the job branch's copy. The checkout, its index and its branch are never touched; when the checkout is on main itself, it still moves to the new commit as today. test/cli.test.mjs ('the agent drafts the plan, a person approves it, and it lands alone', line ~429) asserts that approve on a job's branch is refused; rewrite that part so approve on a job's branch succeeds and leaves the checkout alone, keeping its approve-from-main path. jobs.goal: A live plan view with decisions, in any terminal
jobs.brief: Codex gives gmod no pane, so the person needs one of their own: `gmod watch`, run in a second terminal or a tmux split beside any agent. lib/watch.mjs: on a TTY it draws lib/render.mjs board, and under it the open proposal or decision card, redrawing when `gmod stamp` changes (looked at every second) and syncing with origin every 30 seconds. Keys: up/down move over jobs and signals, enter folds or opens a phase or a job (goal, criteria, files, last journal lines), and on a signal the keys it offers: a approve, c ask for changes (then a typed note), r reject, on an ADR draft a accept and r reject, on a request a typed answer; q quits. A decision goes through lib/decide.mjs decide with via 'watch' and the rev that is on screen, so a proposal that changed since it was drawn is refused and redrawn; decide's refusal under an agent's environment stays as it is, so an agent that starts gmod watch can decide nothing. Without a TTY, `gmod watch` prints the board once and exits. Keep the logic testable without a terminal: a pure step(state, key) that returns the next state and at most one action, and view(state, status, width) that returns lines; the TTY loop only reads keys and writes lines.

done_when.text: the view shows the board and the waiting proposal card, and moving and opening a phase or job changes what is shown
approve from the view decides through gmod decide with via watch and the rev on screen, and is refused when the proposal changed or an agent's environment is set
without a terminal gmod watch prints the board once

jobs.goal: Docs and capabilities say how gmod works in Codex
jobs.brief: Add docs/codex.md: installing the plugin in Codex (the marketplace, `gmod` on PATH, reviewing and trusting the hooks with /hooks), what is the same as in Claude Code (the tools, the refusals, red then green, mcp__gmod__commit, CI), and what differs: no pane, so the plan and proposals are text (gmod board, the card a tool returns) and the person decides in `gmod watch` or with `gmod decide`; no allow-plan; a PreToolUse hook is a guardrail, and CI's gate stays the hard line. Link it from README.md (Install, and 'Works with what you have') and docs/agents.md, and add the Codex limits to docs/limits.md (hooks must be trusted once and again after each gmod upgrade; an untrusted hook is skipped, so nothing is refused locally until it is). lib/capabilities.mjs: add ENFORCES entries of kind 'mod' for the Codex hooks (edits outside the job, the shell rules, the commit gate) naming lib/hook.mjs, and add 'board' to COMMANDS; update test/fixtures/v1 only if a recorded shape gains a field.

gmod capabilities lists what the Codex hooks enforce and the board command

jobs.goal: Release gmod 1.9.0 with Codex support
jobs.brief: Bump to 1.9.0 as 1.8.1 did: npm version 1.9.0 --no-git-tag-version, .claude-plugin/plugin.json and codex/plugin.json by hand, test/release.test.mjs at 1.9.0 (and that codex/plugin.json carries the same version), CHANGELOG.md 1.9.0 entry: gmod in OpenAI Codex (plugin, MCP tools, hooks), gmod board and gmod watch, shell rules tested in CI. After landing: tag v1.9.0, publish the GitHub release, move the installed gmod, tell the open sessions.

jobs.goal: One job's pull request can't finish another job
jobs.brief: A job is done once any commit on main has a subject starting '<id>:' (lib/core.mjs doneJobs), and pull requests land as merge commits, so every commit on a job's branch reaches main. The gate (verify, jobFindings) never looks at those subjects: a commit titled 'b: …' inside job a's pull request marks b done and unblocks whatever waits for it, with none of b's proof. In jobFindings, read the subjects of the non-merge commits in mb..head and fail when one starts with the id of a different job in the base's plan ('names job b, but this pull request is job a's'), or with a prefix gmod writes itself: 'plan:' or 'managed:'. Apply the same to plan, ADR, managed and CI changes: none of their commits may start with a job's id, except a CI change made as that job (isCiJob). In validatePlan, refuse the job ids 'plan' and 'managed' for new plans; a plan already on main that has one keeps loading (report it as a warning in warnings(), not a validation failure). doneJobs itself stays as it is: existing history must keep reading as done.

done_when.text: the gate refuses a job's pull request carrying a commit whose subject names another job, or starts with plan: or managed:
a plan or decision change whose commit subject starts with a job's id is refused
a new job may not be called plan or managed

jobs.goal: Every check must fail without the change
jobs.brief: lib/core.mjs prove() puts the job's code back and passes when at least one criterion fails (`without.some(r => !r.pass)`): a job with five criteria is proven even if four of its checks pass whatever the code does. Require every distinct check command among the job's done_when to fail with the code put back; name each one that still passes in the gate's finding ('"<criterion>" passes without the change: its check proves nothing'). Some criteria are honest guards that hold before and after ('the full status is unchanged'): a done_when entry may say "keeps": true, which must pass both with and without the change and is left out of the must-fail rule; a job needs at least one criterion that isn't a keeps. validatePlan accepts the field and refuses a job whose criteria are all keeps. The local commit gate (gateCommit) is unchanged. warnings() tells the planner when two criteria of one job share a check, since they can only fail together. Jobs already done are not re-judged.

done_when.text: the proof fails, naming the criterion, when one of a job's checks still passes with the code put back
a criterion marked keeps must pass both ways, and a job of only keeps criteria is not a valid plan

jobs.goal: The gate re-runs finished jobs' checks a change touches
jobs.brief: A job's pull request runs only its own checks (lib/core.mjs jobFindings, prove), so it can break what an earlier job proved and still land; only GitLab looks afterwards. In jobFindings, after the proof, run at the pull request's head the checks of jobs already done on the base whose files, tests or the plan's contracts overlap the files this pull request changed (the same globs allowed() and matches() use), each distinct command once and never one the job's own proof just ran. A failing one fails the gate: '"<criterion>" of <job>, proven earlier, fails with this change'. The plan may set "regress": "overlap" (the default), "all" (every done job's checks) or "off"; validatePlan accepts only those. Run them in the proof's scratch checkout before its code is put back, so no second checkout is made, and report how many ran in a passing finding.

done_when.text: a pull request that breaks a finished job's check on files it changed is refused, naming that job and criterion
each distinct command runs once, regress all runs every finished job's checks, and regress off runs none

jobs.goal: The review's verdict is computed, not taken on trust
jobs.brief: ci/review.mjs exits on the model's own `overall` and checks only the answer's shape: a model that fails a criterion but writes overall 'pass' passes, and one that answers no criteria at all passes too. (1) Compute the overall in code: fail if any criterion, tests_are_real, stays_within_goal or ADR verdict is fail; else concern if any is concern; else pass. Print the computed one; when it differs from the model's, say so in the report. Do the same for a governance review from weakens. (2) Coverage: the answer must hold one criteria entry per done_when of the job and one adrs entry per governing ADR id; a missing one counts as unanswered (the existing fail-closed path), naming what is missing. (3) Shortening: a file is treated as generated only when its path says so (zz_generated) or the 'Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.' / controller-gen header is already in the file at the merge base; a new or newly-marked file is shown in full, up to FILE_LIMIT. When any non-data file was cut at FILE_LIMIT, the computed overall is at least concern and the report says the reviewer did not see all of it.

done_when.text: a review whose items include a fail blocks even when the model's overall says pass
an answer missing a criterion or a governing ADR is treated as no answer and stops a blocking review
a new file carrying a generated-code header is shown to the reviewer in full, and a file cut for size makes the overall at least concern

jobs.goal: Checks run without CI's secrets in their environment
jobs.brief: lib/core.mjs runChecks and teardown start `sh -c <check>` with the whole environment of the gmod process. In CI that holds every secret the action was given (action.yml: GMOD_GITHUB_TOKEN, GMOD_FORGE_TOKEN, GMOD_REVIEW_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GMOD_AGENT_KEY, GMOD_APP_KEY; GMOD_TOKEN on the gate step), so a pull request's own test code can read them. Build the environment for checks and teardown from a list instead: PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, LANG, LC_*, TZ, TMPDIR, TERM, CI, NODE_OPTIONS, and whatever the plan names in a new optional "check_env": ["NAME", …] (validatePlan: a list of variable names; a name matching /TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD/i or starting GMOD_ is refused, with the reason). Everything else is left out, in CI and at the desk alike, so a check behaves the same in both. git's own GIT_CONFIG_* variables pass through (the tests' setup relies on them). Say in the gate's report, as an info line, which extra variables the plan passed.

done_when.text: a check sees none of GMOD_TOKEN, GMOD_GITHUB_TOKEN, GMOD_FORGE_TOKEN, GMOD_APP_KEY, GMOD_AGENT_KEY, GMOD_REVIEW_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, in check, prove and the moved-main run
a variable named in the plan's check_env reaches the check, and a secret-like name there is not a valid plan

jobs.goal: Agents in CI hold only a worker's credentials
jobs.brief: lib/agent.mjs runAgent starts Claude Code with bypassPermissions and `{ ...process.env, ...env }`: the agent holds the token that reports gmod / gate and gmod / review and merges, the reviewer's key, the forge token and the App's private key, and ci/action.mjs has written the App's token into .git/config (http extraheader) where the agent can read it. (1) runAgent builds the agent's environment from a list: PATH, HOME, USER, LANG, LC_*, TMPDIR, TERM, CI, the forge's own GITHUB_*/GITEA_*/CI_* run variables, the agent's Anthropic key, IS_SANDBOX, GMOD_AGENT=1 and one worker token (GH_TOKEN, GITEA_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN); nothing else. (2) A new action input `agent-token` (action.yml, passed as GMOD_AGENT_TOKEN): the worker token, for a credential that can push gmod/* branches and open pull requests but has no statuses or administration permission. ci/action.mjs work() and fix() use it for the agent and for the git remote during the agent's run (set the extraheader to the worker token before the agent starts, put the verifier's back after); with no agent-token they fall back to today's token and print one line saying agents hold the verifier's token. (3) ci/gitlab.mjs passes the agent only GMOD_AGENT_TOKEN when the variable is set, the same fallback otherwise. (4) lib/setup.mjs: `gmod setup --agents` leaves 'add GMOD_AGENT_TOKEN' in `left` and doctor reports `missing` for a new check `agent-token` when agents are on without it; the workflow it writes passes agent-token: ${{ secrets.GMOD_AGENT_TOKEN }}.

done_when.text: the agent's environment carries its own key and the worker token and none of the verifier's token, the forge token, the reviewer's key or the App's key
during an agent's run the repository's git config holds the worker token, not the verifier's
setup with agents writes agent-token into the workflow, and doctor says when agents run without one

jobs.goal: Only gmod's App can report the required checks
jobs.brief: gmod / gate and gmod / review are commit statuses, and main's ruleset (lib/ci.mjs githubRuleset) requires them by name only, so any token with statuses: write can report them green. GitHub lets a required check name its source: required_status_checks entries take integration_id. When the repository runs gmod as its App (`gmod setup --app`, app-id in the workflow), githubRuleset adds the App's id to both required checks, and githubProtection (the gate's look at main's live rules) reports the rules as weaker than .gmod/protect.json when an App is configured and a required check isn't pinned to it. .gmod/protect.json gains an optional "app": <id> so the declaration says who reports; protectSpec reads it, and `gmod ci protect` and setup write it. lib/setup.mjs doctor adds a check `check-source`: ok when pinned, missing with the fix `gmod app create` when the repository has no App (the checks can then be reported by anything holding a token with statuses: write). Gitea and GitLab have no such setting: doctor says so in one line and stays ok.

done_when.text: with an App configured the ruleset requires gate and review from that App's id, and the gate refuses when main's live rules don't pin them
doctor reports check-source ok when pinned and missing, with the fix, when there is no App

jobs.goal: The repository lists the keys that may decide
jobs.brief: Who may decide is today a git email and a Decided-By trailer, both of which anyone can write. Give the repository a list of real keys: .gmod/owners, in git's allowed-signers format (one line per owner: an email, then an SSH public key), read from the base branch. New lib/owners.mjs: ownersAt(root, ref) parses it (null when absent; a malformed line is an error naming the line), and signedByOwner(root, commit, ref) answers { ok, by, reason } using `git verify-commit` with gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile pointed at a temporary copy of the base's list, so nothing in the checked-out tree or the person's git config decides. bin/gmod.mjs: `gmod owners` lists them; `gmod owners add <email> <public-key-file>` and `gmod owners remove <email>` write the file and commit it alone as 'owners: add|remove <email>' with the decision trailers, refused under an agent as gmod decide is (lib/decide.mjs agentReason). In lib/core.mjs add .gmod/owners to the files that travel alone as a governance change (CI_FILES) and to what guardPath never lets an agent write. This job only adds the list and its reader; the gate starts requiring signatures in signed-decisions.

done_when.text: a commit signed with a listed SSH key verifies as that owner against the base's list, and an unsigned one or one signed with an unlisted key does not
gmod owners add commits the list alone and is refused under an agent's environment; an agent's edit of .gmod/owners is refused

jobs.goal: The gate lands only decisions an owner signed
jobs.brief: The gate lets a plan, ADR, managed-switch or CI change through when it travels alone and is valid (lib/core.mjs verify), and any gmod/ branch then lands by itself: nothing proves a person approved it. When the base has .gmod/owners (lib/owners.mjs), verify requires every non-merge commit of such a change (modes plan, adr, managed, ci, and a change to .gmod/owners itself) to be signed by a key on the base's list: '<sha> isn't signed by an owner (.gmod/owners): a plan change is a person's decision'. A CI change made as a planned job (isCiJob) is exempt: the plan that planned it was signed. With no .gmod/owners on the base nothing changes except one info line in the gate's report: 'decisions aren't signed here: gmod owners add'. The first commit that adds .gmod/owners is accepted unsigned (there is no list yet to check against) and reported as such. Make the decision commands sign: commitPlan and rebrief (lib/core.mjs), acceptAdr (lib/adr.mjs) and commitSwitch (lib/managed.mjs) pass -S when the repository has an owners file, and when git can't sign they stop with how to set it up (git config gpg.format ssh, user.signingkey), never falling back to an unsigned commit. docs/limits.md: replace the 'against habit, not against intent' paragraph with what signing now holds, and say a hardware-backed key that needs a touch is what stops a program running as you.

done_when.text: with an owners list on the base, an unsigned plan, ADR, managed or CI change is refused by the gate and one signed by a listed key passes
without an owners list the gate behaves as before and says decisions aren't signed
approve, rebrief, adr accept and manage on sign their commit when an owners list exists, and stop rather than commit unsigned

jobs.goal: A job can be marked to wait for a person
jobs.brief: Every job on a gmod/ branch lands by itself once the gate and review pass. Some work should be read by a person first (auth, money, migrations). A job may say "land": "person" (validatePlan: only 'auto', the default, or 'person'). For such a job the checks run and report as always, but gmod doesn't merge it: ci/action.mjs checkAndLand stops after the review with 'passed; <job> waits for a person to merge it' and comments that once on the pull request; landOnGitea doesn't set merge-when-checks-succeed; ci/gitlab.mjs's land step skips it. The job is read from the base's plan, as the gate reads it, so a pull request can't change its own landing. after-merge's stuck report (ci/after-merge.mjs) doesn't call such a pull request stuck for having passed without merging; it says 'waits for a person' once after GMOD_STUCK_HOURS instead. The field shows in `gmod plan` and the proposal card's job lines (lib/core.mjs jobCard) so the person sees it when approving.

done_when.text: a job marked land: person is gated and reviewed but not merged by gmod on GitHub, Gitea or GitLab, and its pull request says it waits for a person
the mark is read from the base's plan, and any other value is not a valid plan

jobs.goal: Codex runs gmod's tools without asking each time
jobs.brief: Found in a live run (codex-cli 0.167, codex exec): every mcp__gmod__ call was refused with 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never', so a headless Codex agent can't work a job at all; interactively the person would be asked on every call. Verified fix: "default_tools_approval_mode": "approve" on the gmod server in codex/mcp.json (then next, claim, status, check and commit ran). Approving gmod's tools by default is safe because each enforces its own rules (claim, red then green, files) and none of them decides for the person. Also from the same run: an agent that was refused an unrelated MCP tool (another server, not gmod) stopped the whole job, following the Codex work skill's 'if anything is denied … stop'. In codex/skills/work/SKILL.md make that rule about what the job needs: a refusal by gmod, its hooks or the sandbox of something the job needs stops the job; a refused tool the job doesn't need is skipped and mentioned. Keep the Claude skill (skills/work) as it is. test/codex-plugin.test.mjs: the gmod server in codex/mcp.json approves its tools by default; the work skill keeps the rule that a refusal by gmod stops the job.

done_when.text: codex/mcp.json approves the gmod server's tools by default
the Codex work skill stops a job on a refusal by gmod, its hooks or the sandbox, and only skips a refused tool the job doesn't need

jobs.goal: A commit with no forge reports the branch ready
jobs.brief: Found in the live Codex run: with origin a plain git path (no GitHub, GitLab or Gitea), `gmod commit` committed and pushed gmod/<job> and then failed with "can't read the forge from origin <path>" when opening the pull request, so the agent reported the job as failed. The work skills promise 'Without a forge (a local origin), mcp__gmod__commit still commits and pushes; say the branch is ready'. In bin/gmod.mjs's commit (and lib/ci.mjs detectForge's callers there), when the forge can't be told from origin, finish successfully after the push with: '<job>: committed and pushed gmod/<job>; origin is no forge gmod knows, so no pull request was opened: the branch is ready'. Any other pull-request error still fails as now. `gmod pr` run on its own keeps its current error.

done_when.text: gmod commit in a repository whose origin is a local path commits, pushes and exits 0 saying the branch is ready and no pull request was opened

jobs.goal: Files changed outside the job by shell are caught
jobs.brief: Found in the live Codex run: asked to add a line to README.md (outside the job), the agent ran `printf 'hello\n' >> README.md` and it went through. gmod's shell rules guard the plan, gmod's records, claims, commits and merges, not ordinary file writes, and Codex edits through the shell far more often than Claude does. Reading every possible write from a command's text can't be done; what changed can be seen afterwards. Add lib/core.mjs strayFiles(root): with a job claimed in this worktree, the changed and untracked paths (as jobPaths reads them) that are outside the job's files, tests and journal, and not in .gitignore. After a shell command: in Codex (lib/hook.mjs, PostToolUse on Bash) return as additionalContext 'gmod: this command changed files outside <job>: <paths>. Put them back (git checkout -- <path>, or remove a new file) before going on; they can't be committed with this job'; in Claude Code (hooks/register.tsx Bash hook, after the command ran) add the same line to the result's context. Only when the set of stray files changed since the last time it was said (kept in the worktree's gmod folder), so it isn't repeated on every step. With no claim, nothing is said (the commit gate already refuses).

done_when.text: after a shell command writes a file outside the claimed job, Codex's PostToolUse answer names the file and how to put it back, once
strayFiles lists changed and new files outside the job's files, tests and journal, and nothing without a claim

jobs.goal: Guards don't block starting a repo or other repos
jobs.brief: Two misfires found while setting up the live Codex test. (1) A new repository can't get its first commit from an agent's session: `gmod init` writes .gmod/plan.json, and the commit gate then refuses every commit ('claim a job first'), yet nothing can be claimed until a plan is committed. The CI gate already treats a base with no plan as ungoverned; make the local gate agree: in lib/core.mjs gateCommit, when HEAD has no commit yet (an unborn branch), allow it with the reason 'the first commit: nothing is governed yet; CI judges what comes after'. (2) The shell rule that refuses writing .gmod/plan.json matches the text anywhere, so it refused writes to a plan in an unrelated scratch repository. Make it about this repository: lib/shell.mjs gains planTargets(cmd, cwd) (the plan paths a command writes, resolved like commitDirs/resolveDir), and the Claude Bash hook (hooks/register.tsx) and Codex's (lib/hook.mjs) refuse only when one resolves to the plan of a repository that is governed (its .gmod/plan.json is committed on HEAD) and isn't allowed by /gmod allow-plan; writesPlan stays exported for compatibility. A plan written for a brand-new repository (no commit yet) is not refused.

done_when.text: the commit gate allows the first commit of a repository with no commits yet, and still refuses an unclaimed commit after that
writing .gmod/plan.json is refused in a governed repository and allowed in one with no committed plan, judged by where the path resolves

phases.title: Fixes
phases.outcome: Setting up and running gmod on GitHub works without hand edits or a person approving each run.

phases.title: Contract for faces
phases.outcome: A face like Skiff can read gmod's version, state and signals as JSON, without the pane.

phases.title: Managed mode
phases.outcome: A repository can opt into managed features (for faces like Skiff) with one switch; without it, gmod behaves exactly as before.

phases.title: Managed guard
phases.outcome: Only a person can switch managed mode, and the switch's own pull request lands through the gate.

phases.title: Upkeep
phases.outcome: CI runs gmod 1.6.0, and gmod's hook refuses only real decisions, not commands that mention them.

phases.title: Surfaces contract
phases.outcome: Every surface (pane, CLI, CI, Skiff, Linear, other agents) can watch one stamp, see the same shared proposals, drafts and red jobs under the same signal ids, and decide through gmod decide.

phases.title: Release 1.7
phases.outcome: gmod 1.7.0 is released once, with the whole contract, and this repository's CI runs it.

phases.title: 1.7 follow-ups
phases.outcome: Small fixes to 1.7 from real use: pane decisions say they came from the pane, tests pass with signing on, the hook refuses commands not text, a stale mod says to restart, and a released branch frees the next claim.

phases.title: Release 1.7.1
phases.outcome: gmod 1.7.1 is released with the five follow-up fixes, and CI runs it.

phases.title: Landed proposals
phases.outcome: An approved proposal never comes back as a stale "no changes" card, and 1.7.2 ships the fix.

phases.title: Requests and decisions
phases.outcome: An agent can ask the person a question and get the answer back, and the person can resolve or re-brief a stuck job, from the pane, the CLI or Skiff.

phases.title: Setup and doctor
phases.outcome: A person's surface like Skiff can set a repository up in one call and read back exactly what is set up, as JSON.

phases.title: Release 1.8
phases.outcome: gmod 1.8.0 is released with requests, resolve, re-brief, setup --json and doctor --json, Skiff has fixtures for each, and CI runs it.

phases.title: Lean status
phases.outcome: An agent's mcp__gmod__status returns what it needs to work (its claim and the open jobs) in a few thousand tokens, however long the plan's history grows.

phases.title: Host-neutral core
phases.outcome: gmod's shell rules, its agent tools and a text view of the plan work without Claude Code.

phases.title: Codex works jobs
phases.outcome: An agent in OpenAI Codex does a gmod job with the same tools and the same refusals as one in Claude Code.

phases.title: Deciding beside Codex
phases.outcome: A person using Codex reads the plan, its phases and proposals as text and decides in a terminal of their own, and gmod 1.9.0 ships it.

phases.title: A truer gate
phases.outcome: The gate and the review hold what they claim: no job is finished by another's pull request, every check is proven, and the verdict is computed in code.

phases.title: Verifier apart from worker
phases.outcome: Code under test and agents in CI never hold the credentials that report the checks or land the work.

phases.title: Provably a person
phases.outcome: A plan, decision or CI change lands only when signed by a key the repository's owners listed, and a job can be marked to wait for a person.
